summary: Defines the SPPI, the adapted subset of SNMP's Structure of Management Information used to write Policy Information Base modules. It is historic.

plainLanguage.summary: SPPI defines how to describe policy data in a consistent form. A PIB module names policy classes, their fields and how an implementation can install or report them.

subtitle: An ASN.1 language for defining policy information that COPS-PR can provision to network devices.

tldr.problem: COPS-PR needs a defined structure for policy information shared between policy decision points and enforcement points. Without a common model, the sender and receiver cannot agree on policy data and its meaning.
tldr.mechanism: SPPI adapts parts of SNMP's Structure of Management Information. It defines PIB modules made of Provisioning Classes, their attributes, and rules for describing instances and conformance.
tldr.outcome: RFC 3159 is Historic. It specifies the language and data model for Policy Information Base modules used with policy provisioning.

today: RFC 3159 is Historic. It defines SPPI, the language used to write Policy Information Base modules for policy provisioning.

sections.title: SPPI and Policy Modules
sections.content:
SPPI is an adapted subset of SNMP's Structure of Management Information (SMI), based on an ASN.1 data definition language. It is used to write Policy Information Base (PIB) modules. The RFC connects this model to COPS-PR, which provisions policy information.

SPPI reuses SMI concepts and tools where possible, but changes some terms to distinguish its definitions from COPS protocol objects. It does not specify how a network decides which policy to use; it defines how policy information is described.
sections.plainLanguage: SPPI is a language for describing policy data, based on the language used for SNMP management information. COPS-PR can carry the data, while SPPI defines its structure.

sections.title: Classes, Instances and Attributes
sections.content:
A Provisioning Class (PRC) defines a table and its row, including the attributes that every instance has. A Provisioning Instance (PRI) is one instance of that row. Unlike SMI, SPPI does not support scalar objects.

A PIB module groups related PRCs and their definitions. It can use textual conventions for reusable types, references between instances, and tags that group instances. An instance identifier identifies a PRI within its class.
sections.plainLanguage: A PRC defines a kind of policy record and the fields it contains. A PRI is one record of that kind, and its attributes hold the record's values.

sections.title: Types and PIB Definitions
sections.content:
SPPI defines the syntax used by PIB modules, including inherited SMI types and the additional Integer64 and Unsigned64 types. A module imports definitions it uses and follows the SPPI rules for identifiers and object assignments.

Each PRC has a table definition and a row definition. The row describes its attributes and their data types. The PIB-INDEX, AUGMENTS and EXTENDS clauses specify how an instance is identified or related to another class.
sections.plainLanguage: SPPI gives each field a defined data type and each class a way to identify its records. Modules can also link one class to another or extend an existing class.

sections.title: Access and Implementation Requirements
sections.content:
The PIB-ACCESS clause says whether a policy class can be installed, reported by a device, both, or included only in reports. Conformance groups collect related attributes. A MODULE-COMPLIANCE definition states the minimum implementation requirements for a PIB module.

The RFC's Security Considerations section says the language itself has no security impact on the Internet. Security for policy delivery is outside the scope of this data-definition language.
sections.plainLanguage: A PIB can state which policy records a controller installs and which a device reports. The RFC says SPPI's language itself has no security impact; it does not define security for delivering policy.
